page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr8i.xlarge is an x86_64 virtual server from the High Clock Speed family, hosted on the KVM hypervisor. The hardware profile features 4 dedicated Intel Xeon 6462C vCPUs operating at a frequency of 3.3 GHz. Memory capacity is provisioned at 32.0 GB, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU that supports memory-heavy computation while maintaining sustained processor performance.

The instance configuration excludes onboard local storage drives, requiring workloads to rely on remote block storage for persistence. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses or discrete GPU accelerators are packaged with the host. Dedicated vCPU allocation ensures that compute resources run free from multi-tenant CPU contention or burst credits.

Cost efficiency stems from the combination of high-frequency enterprise processor cores and large per-core memory capacity without the added cost of attached physical storage or accelerator hardware. The server provides a structured trade-off, shifting persistence to attached volumes while maximizing in-memory headroom. Primary workload fits include relational databases, distributed memory caching, transaction processing engines, and enterprise backend services requiring high single-thread clock speed alongside large memory buffers.

With its dedicated compute allocation, high base clock rate, and substantial memory density, resource tradeoffs focus purely on core processor and RAM allocation, relying on external network volumes for permanent storage. This hardware design is appropriate for memory-demanding, latency-sensitive applications including relational database servers, in-memory caches, and enterprise transactional processing.
